reference: Independent system OpenSSH scp performs only relative local fixture copies; contract cases describe the deliberately bounded local subset.
coverage: Local contents, overwrite/truncation, empty source, destination directory, umask/modes
Same-file path, hardlink and symlink preservation
Local colon/dash paths, missing paths, nonrecursive directories, usage statuses
exclusions: Exactly one local regular-file source and destination; local -r/-p and multiple sources are unsupported.
Remote transport, protocol, option grammar and authentication remain deferred.
No remote peer, network operation, nonregular device or host path is used.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Copy a small regular file whose name contains spaces.
cases.script:
printf 'scp fixture bytes\n' > 'source file'
scp 'source file' 'destination file'

cases.purpose: Overwrite a longer existing destination, then copy an empty file. Follow source/destination file symlinks without replacing the links.
cases.script:
printf 'long destination\n' > dst
printf 'x' > src
scp src dst
: > empty
scp empty empty-copy
ln -s src source-link
scp source-link link-copy
ln -s dst dest-link
scp src dest-link

cases.purpose: Copy into a directory and retain source executable bits subject to umask; an existing destination keeps its mode.
cases.script:
mkdir target
printf 'payload\n' > src
chmod 751 src
scp src target
printf 'old\n' > dst
chmod 600 dst
scp src dst

cases.purpose: A same-path copy must fail without truncating its source.
cases.script:
printf 'keep these bytes\n' > src
scp src src

cases.purpose: Hardlink and symlink aliases must both fail without truncation. Capture each expected failure before checking the effects. Include the same source selected through a destination directory.
cases.script:
printf 'keep linked bytes\n' > src
ln src hard
ln -s src symbolic
a=0; scp src hard || a=$?
[[ $a == 1 ]] || exit 90
b=0; scp src symbolic || b=$?
[[ $b == 1 && $(<src) == 'keep linked bytes' ]] || exit 91
rc=0; scp src . || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && $(<src) == 'keep linked bytes' ]] || exit 92
printf 'same inode preserved\n'

cases.purpose: Explicit ./ and -- keep colon and leading-dash fixture names local.
cases.script:
printf 'local bytes\n' > ./a:b
scp ./a:b ./c:d
printf 'dash bytes\n' > ./-src
scp -- -src -dst

cases.purpose: A missing source returns 1 and leaves an existing destination intact.
An unavailable destination directory returns 1 and leaves the source intact.
Nonrecursive directory copy fails without producing a destination.
Missing operands, unknown options, and a missing port argument all return 1 before file operations.
Local recursion and transport/preservation options are explicitly outside the bounded regular-file contract.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > src
for flag in -r '-p 22' '-P 22'; do
  rc=0; scp $flag src dst || rc=$?
  [[ $rc == 1 && ! -e dst ]] || exit 90
done
printf 'bounded local mode\n'

cases.purpose: Remote upload, download, recursive and remote-to-remote behavior.
Bash type metadata should identify the scp command as a loadable builtin.
Bash help describes the bounded local regular-file interface and remote transport; metadata only.
cases.script:
h=$(help scp)
[[ $h == *'Local mode copies exactly one regular file'* && $h == *'Same-file copies fail without'* && $h == *'Remote SRC or DST'* ]]
printf 'documented scp help
'

cases.purpose: A scp invocation without source and destination operands should follow OpenSSH scp's usage-error status and diagnostics policy.
An unrecognized option should fail before any transfer or filesystem operation.
The -P option without its required port argument should fail before any transport is opened.
Single-file upload and download, including destination naming and transfer option forwarding.
Recursive (-r) upload and download of a small directory tree, including nested files and spaces in relative paths.
